description:
We are XTerra - a small crew of college devs, designers, and troubleshooters from Ukraine, uniting to bridge Earth-level grit with orbital challenges. Our name says it all: 'X' for the unknown exploration, 'Terra' for the ground we stand on.

With a logo that looks like a spin of orbital chaos (honestly, a lot like our Git history), we’re focusing our weekend on the human side of space: translating complex, erratic biometric sensor data into clear, life-saving telemetry. We’re not here to pitch sci-fi fantasies or drop buzzwords; we’re here to tackle the hard stuff - like preventing hypoxia or exhaustion - with solid logic, a user-focused dashboard, and zero over-engineering.
summary:
ASTRA-Med (Autonomous Space Telemetry & Risk Assessment) is a full-stack, offline-first onboard medical console built by Team xterra to help astronauts monitor health, interpret space-specific physiological changes, and make autonomous clinical decisions on deep-space missions.
What we developed: A React/TypeScript mission console paired with a FastAPI/SQLite backend and a hybrid AI/Computer Vision diagnostic engine. The interface features an interactive 8-zone body map, 30-day biometric trend charts, an environment and crisis simulator (Spacecraft, Gateway, Rover, Mars Base; solar flares, CO₂ drift, sleep deficit), gamified daily routines (readiness score, streaks, badges), and an OWLT-aware Ground Flight Surgeon telemetry transmitter. Its diagnostic pipeline combines Gemini Vision (gemini-3.5-flash) with a deterministic offline OpenCV/Tesseract fallback for multi-organ ultrasound analysis, skin/eye inspection, and device LCD OCR.
How it addresses the challenge & why it matters: Grounded in NASA HRP’s 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight and CSA radiation guidelines, ASTRA-Med evaluates vitals against gravity-adjusted thresholds (0g, 0.16g, 0.38g), multi-day deterioration slopes, and immune-radiation synergy, issuing 3-tier escalations (Self-Care, Crew Medical Officer, Flight Surgeon). When Moon-to-Mars communication delays reach 14+ minutes, ASTRA-Med keeps crews safe, proactive, and self-sufficient even without Earth connectivity.
details:
What ASTRA-Med Does & How It Works

ASTRA-Med (Autonomous Space Telemetry & Risk Assessment) is an offline-first onboard medical decision-support console built for deep-space crews. It continuously tracks 8 core biometric and environmental indicators (heart rate, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, daily sleep, mood score, and daily radiation dose in mSv/day) and maps them onto an interactive 8-zone anatomical body model across 4 physiological layers (Cardiovascular, Musculoskeletal, Immune/Radiation, and Neuro/Behavioral).

The workflow operates in four integrated stages:

  1. Context-Aware Monitoring: Crew members switch between 4 mission environments—Space Station (0g, 1.2s OWLT), Lunar/Mars EVA Rover (0.16g/0.38g, 4m OWLT), Planetary Base (7m OWLT), and Mars Spacecraft Transit (0g, 14m 20s OWLT)—automatically adapting physiological thresholds.
  2. Multi-Factor Risk & Trend Evaluation: Rather than waiting for static red alarms, the risk engine computes 5–14 day linear regression slopes (np.polyfit) to detect creeping sleep-HR drift, mood decline, or glucose rise, and checks cross-hazard interactions such as NASA HRP Immune–Radiation Synergy.
  3. Multimodal Medical Imaging: Astronauts upload or capture portable ultrasound frames (ocular SANS, lung B-lines, cardiac, renal), skin/eye photos, or medical device LCD screens. Every image passes brightness and Laplacian sharpness checks, routes to Gemini 3.5 Flash for structured ROI triage (<7s budget), and automatically falls back to a deterministic offline OpenCV + Tesseract OCR pipeline when offline.
  4. Autonomous Triage & OWLT Uplink: Every evaluation outputs a dynamic Readiness Score (5–100), plain-language space-hazard explanations, 3-tier clinical escalation (Self-Care, Crew Attention, Flight Surgeon), gamified countermeasure tasks, and a compact JSON Telemetry Packet stamped with exact One-Way Light Time (OWLT) delivery latency.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Crew Autonomy Under Signal Delay: Eliminates reliance on real-time Earth consultation during 14+ minute Mars transit delays or solar blackouts.
  • Early Preventive Intervention: Catches gradual physiological drift and syndrome coupling (SANS, radiation-amplified infection risk, CO₂ scrubber drift) before acute medical emergencies develop.
  • Dual Space & Earth Value: Built for Artemis, Lunar Gateway, and Mars missions, and immediately transferable to isolated terrestrial settings such as Antarctic stations, submarines, maritime vessels, and disaster zones.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Stack

  • Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS v4, Recharts, Lucide Icons.
  • Backend & Database: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, Uvicorn, SQLite in WAL mode (100% local persistence).
  • AI & Computer Vision: Google GenAI SDK (gemini-3.5-flash), OpenCV (opencv-python-headless), NumPy, Pillow, PyTesseract (Tesseract OCR).
  • DevOps & QA: Docker Compose, Pytest (21 automated API, risk, and vision tests), Ruff linter, GitHub Actions CI.

How Our Project Is Creative

  • Hybrid Online/Offline Vision Router: Seamlessly pairs cloud multimodal LLM reasoning with deterministic local OpenCV/Tesseract fallback (multi-organ ultrasound ROI detection, HSV erythema masking, and range-guarded LCD OCR) so diagnostics never fail without internet.
  • Space-Adjusted Synergy & Crisis Simulator: Combines gravity-adapted norms, multi-day regression slopes, live fault injection (Solar Particle Events, CO₂ drift, sleep deficit), and behavioral gamification (streaks and 6 NASA-themed badges) in one cohesive flight console.

Factors Our Team Considered

We grounded every rule in NASA’s Human Research Program (5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight), CSA radiation guidelines, and Artemis Standard Measures—balancing clinical accuracy, cognitive ergonomics for stressed non-physician crews, strict Deep Space Network bandwidth limits (~1.4 KB uplink packets), and zero-cloud reliability.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI) / AI Disclosure

- Built-in Product AI: ASTRA-Med integrates Google Gemini Vision (gemini-3.5-flash) via the google-genai SDK for multimodal medical image triage, paired with a deterministic OpenCV + Tesseract OCR offline fallback.

- Development & Data Assistance: AI coding and writing assistants (Google Antigravity / Gemini, Claude) were used to assist with software scaffolding, debugging, unit test generation, documentation editing, presentation layout, and structuring the synthetic 24-day mission telemetry seed dataset (data/seed_30days.json) and threshold reference files (data/nasa_hrp_rules.json) based on public NASA HRP and CSA publications. All synthetic demo images in data/demo_samples/ are programmatically generated via scripts/generate_demo_images.py using Pillow/NumPy.
